body_text: SYDNEY (July 20, 2026) — AECOM, the trusted global infrastructure leader, today announced its appointment as the lead design consultant for Stage 2 of the New Richmond Bridge project, supporting Transport for New South Wales and the lead contractor, Fulton Hogan. The partnership will design and deliver a new, taller flood-resilient bridge over the Hawkesbury River at North Richmond, maintaining community connectivity during flooding events. “We see bridges as more than transport infrastructure — they are enduring structures of engineering, science and design that must perform under the forces of nature while connecting people, places and economies,” said Julian Small, AECOM’s managing director for transportation in Australia and New Zealand. “Our multidisciplinary bridge team brings technical excellence to deliver resilient structures that support long-term connectivity for the community.” The new bridge will feature two lanes in each direction to support future population growth, and is intended to sit around 10 metres higher than the existing structure to better withstand flood events. The project will ease congestion in Richmond by creating a new bypass south of the town centre, and the existing bridge will be converted into a walking and cycling connection for active travel across the Hawkesbury River. “It is incredibly exciting to be part of a project that will deliver lasting benefits for the Hawkesbury community,” said Rezarta Rushitaj, the project’s design manager and AECOM’s technical excellence leader for transportation in Australia and New Zealand. “We will preserve and celebrate the heritage character of the existing Richmond Bridge by repurposing it as a dedicated shared user path, removing vehicular traffic and creating a safe and attractive space for pedestrians and cyclists.” The bridge will also feature lookout and rest areas, allowing the community to enjoy river views while strengthening active transport connections to nearby Hannah Park. The New Richmond Bridge project will improve flood resilience, reduce congestion and crashes, enhance connectivity to Sydney’s road network, and support long-term community and economic growth across the region. About AECOM AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com .

title: How to improve visibility and coordination across your mobile release process
summary: Most mobile teams accept poor release visibility as the cost of doing business. But the coordination tax compounds fast and the fix starts with infrastructure, not effort.
body_text: Automate the coordination tax A huge proportion of coordination work in mobile releases is mechanical: reminding people about deadlines, bumping version numbers, tagging tickets, generating changelogs, posting status updates to Slack, and submitting builds to TestFlight. Every manual step can lead to mistakes. Things may get dropped, delayed, or done inconsistently. Visibility gets foggier with each misstep, especially when speed increases. An understandable urge is to automate as much of the release process (and its reporting) as possible. Unfortunately, this often doesn’t actually ease the pain. Seventy-five percent of teams regularly invest in automation and scripting for their release processes to fix these issues. However, these teams still report ongoing challenges with wasted time, high incident rates, and unpredictability. The reason is what the report calls the automation paradox . Most teams have improved their CI/CD pipelines and build scripts. However, these tools handle specific tasks and don’t unify the release workflow. Engineers are still manually bridging gaps in a fragmented toolchain. They jump between Jira, Slack, CI dashboards, App Store Connect, and spreadsheets. This juggling is needed to fully understand what's happening with each release. The tools are automated, but the coordination between the tools is not. More automation isn’t the goal here, integration automation is. This means steps trigger automatically as the release moves through stages. The right people get notified in the right channels, at the right time. Information flows through your toolchain without needing manual relays. When a build passes QA, the next steps should kick off without someone manually triggering them. When a submission gets rejected, the right people should be notified right away. No one should need to check a dashboard or send a Slack message. Instrument your rollouts with release health metrics Visibility doesn't end at app store submission. The rollout phase is crucial for release coordination and you need real-time signals to decide if you should continue, pause, or roll back. Without health metrics, you’re flying blind at the most critical stage. Four categories of metrics matter here: Stability covers crash-free user rates, crash-free session rates, and out-of-memory crashes. Performance covers app startup time, network latency, and ANR rates. User behavior covers regressions in key flows such as signups, purchases, and core engagement metrics. Store signals cover app store rating trends and review sentiment. The key is not just having these metrics, but surfacing them in the same place as your release status. When health metrics are displayed alongside release progress, engineering managers and product leads can see the signals clearly. This arrangement makes diagnosing problems easier. It also helps them decide whether to pause or accelerate the process. You’re not cross-referencing five tabs to determine if a crash spike correlates with a specific build, a late cherry-pick, or a rollout threshold that you just crossed. Good release tools cut down the time from "something's wrong" to "we know what's wrong and who's fixing it." They provide visibility when it counts. More than 75% of mobile teams face issues needing hotfixes about every fourth release, based on our data. That's a predictable disruption cycle, which means most of this pain isn't unavoidable, it's unmitigated. Better visibility, health-gated rollout controls, and faster triage can turn midnight emergencies into daytime issues. The team can then handle these situations with confidence, not panic. Frequency of incidents leading to delayed features or hotfixes. Building releases that are boring (in the best way) If you're a senior engineering manager focusing more on release status than product strategy, working harder on the current process won't help. It's to build in visibility that makes coordination easy to track and manage. That means a single source of truth that any stakeholder can read in five seconds. It means clear ownership at every stage, with rotation that distributes knowledge across the team. It means automation that connects your toolchain rather than adding more tools to juggle. It means health metrics that surface the rollout signal your whole team needs to make decisions with confidence. And, finally, it means documentation and processes that hold up as the team grows, not just today. The goal is releases that are boring. So routine and well-instrumented that they barely need active coordination. That's not a low bar. It's the highest one. See how Runway delivers better visibility for your whole team with one shared, unified view → Explore the sandbox ‍ FAQ What is the biggest obstacle to visibility in a mobile release process? The biggest obstacle is fragmented information. Release status information is often scattered across Jira tickets, Slack threads, spreadsheets, and individual engineers' heads. When there's no centralized, always-current view of where a release stands, stakeholders and engineers can't get the full picture without pinging someone directly. The fix is a dashboard that acts as a single source of truth to surface phase, blockers, build metadata, app store submission status, and rollout progress in one place. How do you improve visibility and coordination across a mobile release process? You improve visibility and coordination across your mobile release process by establishing a single source of truth for release status, defining clear ownership at every stage, automating routine handoffs and notifications, and instrumenting your rollouts with health metrics the whole team can see. The goal is moving from scattered, tribal-knowledge-driven releases to a structured workflow where every stakeholder–engineering to QA to product to leadership–can see exactly where things stand without having to ask. What release health metrics should you monitor during a mobile app rollout? The four categories to monitor during a staged rollout are stability (crash-free user rate, crash-free session rate, out-of-memory crashes), performance (app startup time, network latency, ANR rates), user behavior (regressions in key flows like signups or purchases), and store signals (rating trends, review sentiment). These metrics should be visible to the whole team alongside release status (not siloed in a monitoring tool only the on-call engineer checks) so decisions about pausing or accelerating the rollout don't bottleneck on one person.

title: WhatsApp Message Limits & Tiers Explained: 2026 Guide
summary: Master WhatsApp message limits and tiers. Learn about the 6-hour re-evaluation cycle, shared portfolio caps, and how to scale your quality rating in 2026.
body_text: Hitting your WhatsApp tier limit is only the first bottleneck; blasting a stale list to force an upgrade will freeze your account instead. The caps themselves are the simple part. WhatsApp limits you to 1,000, 10,000, or 100,000 unique users per rolling 24 hours . As of October 2025 those limits are shared across your entire Business Portfolio, and in 2026 Meta re-evaluates your account standing on a strict 6-hour cycle . What that cycle does to an account trying to grow is the part nobody writes down. The median guide on this topic celebrates reach and open rates, advising merchants that when numbers drop, the solution is simply to “send more” to reach a higher tier. Most ignore the failure path a merchant actually hits on send #1. This is a diagnostic manual for managing Meta’s limits and understanding why messages fail to deliver even when you have capacity remaining. What are the WhatsApp Business messaging tiers? Your messaging limit dictates how many unique users your business can initiate a conversation with in a 24-hour period. Tier Limit (Unique Users / Rolling 24h) The 2026 Mechanic Tier 1 1,000 The starting cap for all verified business numbers. Tier 2 10,000 Requires sustained volume and a high quality rating. Tier 3 100,000 The threshold for scaling mid-market D2C broadcasts. The “rolling 24-hour” mechanic means your limit doesn’t reset at midnight. If you message 500 users at 4:00 PM, you only have 500 sends remaining until 4:00 PM the next day. Historically, merchants bypassed these limits by registering multiple phone numbers. The October 2025 update closed this loophole: limits are now shared at the Business Portfolio level . Adding a new number to your portfolio no longer grants a separate 1,000-message allowance. With the side door shut, the only way up is to earn the next tier. That is where most accounts break. Why do forced tier upgrades fail? Sent isn’t delivered — and the gap between those two words is where the tier ladder actually lives. Merchants try to force an upgrade by maxing out their daily limit to hit Meta’s volume thresholds. But because Meta re-evaluates limits every six hours , a high-volume send to a stale list generates blocks and spam reports that tank your quality rating before the cycle finishes. When the rating drops to “Flagged” or “Low,” the upgrade path freezes. Merchants routinely misattribute this delivery loss to WhatsApp’s platform capacity rather than fixing the actual broken rung: their list hygiene. So when delivery drops, don’t start at the platform. Diagnosing it means working down a ladder, one rung at a time — each rung fails silently, and each fails at a different layer: List hygiene: Are the numbers active, and did they explicitly opt-in to WhatsApp? A pre-checked SMS box or a standard checkout phone field isn’t a WhatsApp opt-in; messaging these numbers violates Meta’s commerce policy and guarantees high block rates. Meta ecosystem caps: Has the user received too many marketing messages from other brands today? Template class: Is your message categorized correctly (Marketing vs. Utility)? Sender reputation: Is your phone number quality rating currently High, Medium, or Low? The math of a forced upgrade: Say you push 1,000 messages at an unengaged list to trigger a Tier 2 upgrade, and 15% of them get blocked (that block rate is an assumption — use your own historical SMS decay rate, not a number off a blog). 1,000 messages × 15% blocks = 150 immediate negative signals. 1,000 messages × your own marketing template rate = what those signals cost you. You spent a full broadcast budget to manufacture 150 spam reports. Meta’s algorithms process those negative signals in the next 6-hour re-evaluation cycle , downgrade your quality rating, and freeze your tier. The volume is the trigger, but the quality rating is the gate. What is the difference between service windows and business-initiated limits? Rung one is list hygiene, and the cheapest way to keep a list healthy is to stop broadcasting at it — because not every message you send is drawn from the same budget. Two accounts on the same tier can have very different room to work with, and the difference is who spoke first. Once a customer replies to your business, a 24-hour customer service window opens . Inside this window, you can send free-form replies, and these messages don’t count against your business-initiated tier limits. Outside of this 24-hour window, template messages are the only type sendable . If a user enters your WhatsApp chat via a Click-to-WhatsApp (CTWA) ad, the free-form window extends to 72 hours . The extended window is for answering objections and guiding a purchase, not just pushing a daily discount code. What is a realistic WhatsApp read rate? Capacity is only half the question. The other half is what happens to the messages that do go out — and this is where most WhatsApp forecasts are built on a number nobody can source. The widely-repeated “98% open rate” has no published methodology — it traces to WhatsApp’s own early marketing copy . We don’t use it to project campaign ROI, and it isn’t the standard your account should be held to. The measured opt-in read rate for WhatsApp broadcasts is ~68% . Delivery and read rates split sharply based on list age: fresh lists routinely see 90%+ read rates, while stale lists drop to 65-75% . Never promise a delivery rate — not to your team, and not in a forecast. Delivery is Meta’s call, re-evaluated on the 6-hour cycle against signals you only partly control. List hygiene is the one rung of the ladder you fully own; the quality rating it earns isn’t yours to guarantee. Automating compliance and sender reputation Which leaves you managing the one rung you own — and doing it by hand. Broadcast pacing, template compliance and list hygiene are a full-time job, and every hour you don’t spend on them is charged to your Meta sender reputation. BusinessOnBot is the D2C automation layer for Shopify. Instead of batch-and-blast campaigns that jeopardize your tier status, the platform protects your sender reputation by running targeted, intent-based flows—like abandoned checkout recovery and anonymous visitor recovery. By messaging users based on immediate site intent rather than stale lists, you maintain the high quality rating required to scale your messaging tiers. title: Japanese Drama Series 'S&X' Unveils Main Trailer, Key Art and Stills Ahead of August 20 Premiere
summary: Netflix has released the main trailer, key art, and stills for S&X, the new Japanese drama series starring Kento Nakajima, premiering August 20.
body_text: Netflix has released the main trailer, key art, and stills for S&X , the new Japanese drama series starring Kento Nakajima, premiering August 20. Based on Motoo Tada’s manga S&X: The Confession of Therapist Ichito Shimotori (serialized by Kodansha in Morning magazine), the series is set at Shimotori Clinic, where sex therapist Ichito Shimotori treats patients wrestling with deeply personal struggles they can’t bring themselves to tell anyone else — sexless relationships, erectile dysfunction, sex addiction, sexual trauma, and more. Even when he’s met with snickers and prejudice, Shimotori handles each patient with sincerity and unwavering care through counseling. Yet he, too, secretly carries his own unresolved pain… Kento Nakajima , a longtime fixture of Japan’s entertainment scene, breaks new ground as Shimotori, a therapist who steadfastly supports clients carrying all kinds of sexual worries. This marks his second leading role in a Netflix production, following the bittersweet romance Love Like the Falling Petals . Yuko Araki plays the woman who crosses paths with Shimotori in a fateful reunion. They are joined by a stellar ensemble spanning generations, including Ryota Miura , Sawako Fujima , Aoi Nakamura , Rinka Kumada , Sayaka Yamaguchi , Yūsuke Santamaria , and Shiro Sano . Director Shogo Kusano , known for fresh, emotionally rich youth and romance dramas, takes a premise that could easily tip into sensationalism and turns it into something more grounded: an adult drama about real people navigating work, love, and sexuality — one that resonates deeply with anyone who has ever struggled with intimacy. By treating sexuality as something deeply connected to how we express love and how we see our own self-worth, not just biology, this story invites viewers to re-examine their relationships and themselves, and to confront what it truly means to love. S&X is a love story for every adult carrying their own quiet worries. The series premieres August 20, only on Netflix. title: A Buzz on your phone
body_text: Buzz is a new kind of workspace where humans and agents collaborate side by side. But unlike the agents, the humans sometimes leave their computers. To help them stay connected when they do, Buzz is also an app on iOS and Android . On the surface, Buzz looks a lot like other apps humans use to communicate with coworkers. But under the hood it's different, and for a good reason. The thing about agents Unlike humans, agents will do nearly anything they're asked. To protect ourselves from destructive actions they could be asked to take, we usually limit who is allowed to talk to the agent and what the agent is capable of doing. In ChatGPT or Claude, only you talk to your agent, and the agent's actions are often limited by permission requests and sandboxing. When you use an agentic Slack bot, the agent usually runs in a cloud environment that acts as the sandbox. And an agent that has access to your data and permissions usually listens only to you on Slack. The agent trusts Slack to authenticate your messages as coming from you, and also trusts Slack itself not to impersonate you in order to control your agent. Agents without trust Buzz is different. Buzz agents typically run on the same computer a human uses, outside any sandbox, with --dangerously-skip-permissions . This makes them powerful and nearly configuration-free, inheriting the .md s, skills, and credentials of that computer. But this also means the agent can do anything, and security rests entirely on restricting who can tell it what to do. And whereas Slack bots rely on their Slack hooks to know who is talking to them, Buzz agents cannot trust Buzz relays in the same way. Buzz enables anyone to host a relay, administer it as they please, and even modify its source . At the same time, Buzz allows anyone to connect their agents to any relay without offering control over their computer to other parties who participate on, control, or compromise the relay. How? Buzz accomplishes all this through public-key cryptography. The details could fill another blog post, but briefly: agents act only on messages that are signed with a private key held by their owner. That key is never seen by relays or other parties. Taking it with you What does this mean for Buzz running on a phone? It doesn't host agents, but it must be able to message and control agents running elsewhere, without relying on a trusted backend as most mobile apps do. And it shouldn't stop working when a laptop lid somewhere is closed, as some "remote control" features do. I should always be able to leave messages for my agents to find when my laptop wakes up, and for my human collaborators to see immediately. For those reasons, we made the mobile app a full-fledged Buzz. It signs messages, connects directly to relays, and is designed to limit the identifying data those relays and other intermediaries can observe. Below are a few specifics. Pairing The Buzz mobile app preserves the identity you create in the desktop app by reusing the same key pair. The first and last thing you do to "sign in" to the mobile app is point it at a QR code in the desktop app. Loading image... Done. In the future we could support using the mobile app independently of any desktop app, generating a key pair directly on the phone. Privacy The mobile app is designed to keep private and identifying data on the phone. At the time of writing it ships with no analytics SDKs, and it strips metadata such as geolocation from image attachments before upload, so that data is not unintentionally exposed to the relay. You can verify these properties in the mobile source , which lives in the same open source repository as Buzz's desktop app and relay. Push Buzz's push notifications are implemented according to our draft standard ( NIP-PL ), under which the app registers separately with relays and a push gateway. The protocol is designed so that: Relays do not see the device token, which could be used to correlate different identities (public keys) belonging to the same person. The push gateway does not see public keys, message content, or metadata from the relay. Nor the identity of the relay itself, which would associate the device with the relay. Transitively, Apple's and Google's push services also see none of that data. NIP-PL itself may be the topic of a future post. Until next time We're using the iOS and Android apps ourselves to build Buzz, and we hope you find them useful too. We've been updating them every few days with new capabilities and fixes. Stay tuned.

title: The Future of ERP Systems: Trends Shaping the Next Era of Enterprise Solutions
summary: The rise of AI-enabled ERPs and automation platforms is reshaping the market, offering mid-market solutions that promise efficiency without the traditional complexity. Yet, the challenge remains: how to integrate these technologies seamlessly into existing operations.
body_text: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems have long been the backbone of organisational efficiency, serving as the central hub for data and process management. However, the landscape of ERP systems is rapidly evolving, driven by technological advancements and changing business needs. This article delves into the current state of ERP systems, the challenges faced during implementations, and the future trajectory of AI-enabled ERPs. Versori recently hosted an ERP thought leadership panel, to draw back the curtain on the real challenges and success stories of ERP implementation projects. The Panel of ERP Experts: Erin Barton , VP of Tech at TripleBolt.io, on managing complex ERP projects and avoiding common pitfalls. ‍ Will Jackson , COO at Versori, on how improved data connectivity turns ERP from a back-office tool into a growth engine. George Goodfellow , Head of Growth at Versori, on how ERP and integration strategies directly impact scalability, customer experience, and long-term commercial success. Key Takeaways: The Need for ERP Systems The decision to implement an ERP system is not solely dependent on the size of a business. Instead, it hinges on the complexity of operations and the need for streamlined communication and data management. Smaller companies might find themselves in greater need of an ERP due to increasing regulatory demands and the necessity for accurate reporting. The key is recognising when the lack of a unified data entry and exit point is hindering growth. The Evolution of ERP Solutions The market has seen a surge in mid-market solutions and AI-enabled ERPs, offering alternatives to traditional systems. These new entrants aim to automate processes and reduce the complexity associated with ERP implementations. However, the integration of these systems requires a deep understanding of diverse SaaS products and the ability to adapt to various business functions. Overcoming Implementation Challenges ERP implementations are notorious for exceeding budgets and timelines. This is often due to a lack of understanding of the company's future needs and the assumption that a one-size-fits-all solution will suffice. Successful implementations require a clear mapping of current processes and future goals, along with a willingness to embrace a diverse ecosystem of software solutions. The Role of AI in ERP AI is increasingly being integrated into ERP systems, offering the potential for significant efficiency gains. However, the adoption of AI must be approached with caution, ensuring that it is used as an accelerant rather than a replacement for sound business processes. Companies must focus on real use cases that drive business value rather than adopting AI for its novelty. The Importance of Consulting Despite the rise of technology, the role of consultants remains crucial. They provide the external perspective needed to challenge internal assumptions and guide companies through the complex landscape of ERP transformations. The emphasis is on building a technology solution that aligns with the company's strategic goals and future aspirations. ‍ In conclusion, ERP systems remain a critical component of enterprise operations, but their implementation and evolution require careful planning and execution. By understanding the challenges and opportunities presented by AI and other technological advancements, organizations can better position themselves for success in the ever-evolving business landscape. body_text: Insights & Resources Employee Termination Process in India: Legal Steps, Notice & Settlement Guide July 22, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet What Is Employee Termination? Employee termination is the formal process of ending an employment relationship between an employer and an employee. It can be initiated by either party — the employer (dismissal, retrenchment, layoff) or the employee (resignation, retirement). In every case, specific legal procedures must be followed to ensure the termination is valid and enforceable under Indian law. In India, the termination process is primarily governed by: • Industrial Relations Code 2020 (effective 21 November 2025) — replaced the Industrial Disputes Act 1947 and covers workers in industrial establishments. • Shops & Establishments Act — state-specific legislation governing employees in commercial establishments, shops, and offices. • Individual employment contracts — terms agreed upon at the time of hiring, including notice period, probation clauses, and separation procedures. Why Does the Process Matter? Wrongful termination in India can result in reinstatement orders by the Labour Court, full back wages from the date of termination, monetary penalties for the employer, and lasting reputational damage. Following the legally prescribed process protects both the employer and the employee. Whether you are an HR manager handling an employee exit for the first time, a small business owner navigating compliance, or an employee wanting to understand your rights, this guide walks you through every aspect of the employee termination process in India — from legal framework and step-by-step procedures to settlement calculations and ready-to-use letter templates. Types of Termination in India Not all terminations are the same. The type of termination determines the notice requirements, compensation obligations, and legal procedures that apply. Here is a comprehensive overview of every category recognised under Indian law: Type Reason Notice Required Compensation Voluntary Resignation Employee chooses to leave As per contract (30–90 days) Nil (F&F settlement applies) Termination for Cause Proven misconduct after inquiry No notice needed if dismissed No retrenchment compensation Poor Performance Consistent underperformance despite PIP Yes, after PIP process As per contract Retrenchment Economic or business reasons 1 month notice or pay in lieu 15 days avg. pay per year of service Layoff Temporary suspension of work Layoff compensation applies 50% of basic + DA for layoff period Probation Termination During probation period 7–30 days or as per offer letter Nil End of Contract Fixed-term contract expires No notice (end date applies) Pro-rata gratuity and bonus Retirement Reaching retirement age (58–60) Advance intimation by employer Gratuity + PF + leave encashment Each of these categories has distinct legal implications. This guide focuses primarily on employer-initiated termination — particularly termination for misconduct, retrenchment, and the full and final settlement process, as these are the areas where compliance errors are most common and consequences most severe. Legal Framework: Key Laws Governing Termination India’s employee termination laws have been consolidated under the new Labour Codes, which came into effect in late 2025. Understanding which law applies to your establishment and your employees is the first step toward compliant termination. 1. Industrial Relations Code 2020 (Effective 21 November 2025) This is the primary legislation governing termination of workers in factories, mines, plantations, and other industrial establishments. It replaced the Industrial Disputes Act 1947 and brought significant changes: • Standing Orders: Establishments with 300 or more workers must have certified standing orders that define misconduct, disciplinary procedures, and termination rules. • Retrenchment threshold raised: Only establishments with 300+ workers (up from 100) need prior government permission for retrenchment, layoff, or closure. • Fixed-term employees: Entitled to the same benefits as permanent employees, including pro-rata gratuity regardless of service length. • Dispute resolution: Grievance Redressal Committee mandatory in establishments with 20+ workers. 2. Shops & Establishments Act (State-Specific) Each Indian state has its own Shops & Establishments Act covering employees in commercial establishments, shops, offices, restaurants, theatres, and similar workplaces. These laws prescribe: • Notice period requirements for termination • Working hours, leave entitlements, and overtime • Conditions under which termination is permissible • Registration and record-keeping obligations for employers Since these laws vary by state, employers must check the specific provisions applicable in their state of operation. 3. Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 / Code on Social Security 2020 Gratuity is payable to every employee who has completed five or more years of continuous service (or pro-rata for fixed-term contract employees under the new codes). The gratuity formula, tax exemption limits, and payment timelines are discussed in detail in the Gratuity on Termination section below. 4. Code on Wages 2019 This code mandates that when an employee is terminated or resigns, all wages due must be settled within two working days of the last working day. This includes salary for days worked, leave encashment, bonus, and any other dues. Failure to comply can result in penalties and legal action against the employer. Step-by-Step Termination Process for Misconduct Termination for misconduct is the most legally sensitive type of termination. If the procedure is not followed correctly, the termination can be challenged in court and overturned. Below is the legally compliant seven-step process that every employer must follow: Step 1: Document the Misconduct Before any action is taken, the employer must collect and preserve evidence of the alleged misconduct. This includes: • CCTV footage, access logs, or digital records • Emails, chat messages, or written correspondence • Witness statements with dates and details • Attendance records, performance data, or audit findings Ensure the act constitutes “misconduct” as defined in the company’s standing orders, employee handbook, or employment contract. Common examples include theft, fraud, insubordination, habitual absenteeism, and violation of safety norms. Step 2: Issue a Show Cause Notice A show cause notice is a formal written document that: • Describes the alleged misconduct with specific dates, incidents, and evidence references • Asks the employee to explain why disciplinary action should not be taken • Provides 7 to 15 days to respond in writing The notice must be delivered personally with an acknowledgement signature, or sent via registered post with acknowledgement due (RPAD). Verbal warnings do not constitute a valid show cause notice. Step 3: Review the Employee’s Response Once the employee submits their written response: • If the explanation is satisfactory: Close the matter. Issue a written warning if appropriate and place it on record. • If the explanation is not satisfactory: Proceed to a formal domestic inquiry. Do not skip this step — direct termination without an inquiry is the most common ground for wrongful termination claims. Step 4: Conduct a Domestic Inquiry A domestic inquiry (also called a departmental inquiry) is a quasi-judicial proceeding conducted within the organisation. The procedure includes: • Appoint an Inquiry Officer: Must be impartial, typically from a different department or an external person. • Frame charges: Clearly articulate each charge of misconduct. • Allow the employee to defend: The employee has the right to present evidence, cross-examine management witnesses, and bring a co-worker as a defence representative (an external lawyer is generally not permitted). • Maintain records: Detailed minutes of every hearing session must be recorded and signed by all parties. • Inquiry report: The Inquiry Officer submits findings and recommendations to the management. Step 5: Management Decision Based on the inquiry report, the management (typically the disciplinary authority) must: • Review the findings objectively • If misconduct is proved: Issue a termination order. The punishment must be proportionate to the misconduct — courts frequently overturn dismissals where a lesser penalty would have been appropriate. • If misconduct is not proved: Reinstate the employee with a clean record. Any suspension period must be treated as duty, with full wages paid. Step 6: Issue the Termination Letter The termination letter is the formal document that ends the employment. It must include: • Effective date of termination • Reference to the domestic inquiry, its findings, and the management’s decision • Full and final settlement details and the timeline for payment • Instructions for return of company assets (laptop, phone, ID card, access cards) Step 7: Complete Full & Final Settlement Under the Code on Wages 2019, all dues must be settled within two working days of the employee’s last working day. The settlement includes payment of all salary, leave encashment, gratuity (if applicable), bonus, reimbursements, and any other contractual dues — minus recoverable amounts such as notice period shortfall, outstanding loans, and unreturned assets. The detailed calculation of F&F settlement is covered in the next section. Notice Period Rules for Termination The notice period is the advance intimation that either party must give before ending the employment. The length of the notice period depends on the employee’s category, the applicable law, and the terms of the employment contract. Employee Category Typical Notice Period Legal Basis Probationary Employee 7–30 days Appointment / Offer letter Confirmed Employee (Private Sector) 30–90 days Employment contract Workman (Industrial Establishment) 1 month (30 days) Industrial Relations Code 2020 Manager / Senior Executive 60–90 days Employment contract Fixed-Term Contract Employee As per contract or till end date Contract terms Notice Period Pay in Lieu Either party can choose to pay salary for the notice period instead of requiring the employee to serve it. This is known as “pay in lieu of notice.” • Employer terminates without notice: Must pay the employee’s full salary for the applicable notice period. • Employee resigns without serving notice: The employer can recover the notice period salary from the employee’s F&F settlement. Important: Some employment contracts allow the employer to waive the notice period entirely. Always check the specific contract terms before making deductions. Full & Final Settlement: Components & Calculation The full and final settlement (commonly called F&F) is the complete financial reckoning between the employer and the employee at the time of separation. Under the Code on Wages 2019, this must be completed within two working days of the last working day. F&F Formula Net F&F Payable = Total Payable Components − Total Recoverable Components Payable Components 1. Salary for days worked in the last month (pro-rata calculation) 2. Leave encashment: Earned leave balance multiplied by the daily wage rate 3. Gratuity: If 5+ years of service (formula: 15 × last drawn salary × years of service ÷ 26) 4. Bonus: Pro-rata entitlement under the Payment of Bonus Act, if applicable 5. Retrenchment compensation: If termination qualifies as retrenchment (15 days average pay per completed year) 6. Notice period pay: If the employer terminates without serving notice 7. Pending reimbursements: Any approved expense claims, incentives, or variable pay due Recoverable Components 1. Notice period recovery: If the employee does not serve the required notice period 2. Outstanding loan balance: Any salary advance or company loan 3. Advance salary recovery: Over-credited salary amounts 4. Training bond amount: If applicable and the bond is legally enforceable 5. Unreturned company assets: Value of laptop, phone, ID card, or other assets not returned 6. Excess leave adjustment: Salary deduction for leave taken beyond entitlement F&F Settlement: Worked Example Let us calculate the full and final settlement for a typical employee scenario: Employee Profile Name: Rahul Sharma | Designation: Marketing Executive Monthly Salary: Rs 50,000 | Service: 3 years | Earned Leave Balance: 15 days Exit Type: Voluntary resignation | Notice Period: 30 days (served in full) Days Worked in Last Month: 20 out of 30 Payable Component Calculation Amount (Rs) Salary for days worked (20 days) 50,000 / 30 × 20 33,333 Leave encashment (15 EL days) 50,000 / 30 × 15 25,000 Gratuity Not eligible (< 5 years) 0 Bonus (pro-rata) Annual bonus pro-rated 8,333 Total Payable 66,666 Recoverable Component Amount (Rs) Notice period recovery Nil (full notice served) Outstanding loans / advances Nil Unreturned company assets Nil Total Recoverable 0 Net Full & Final Settlement Amount Rs 66,666 (Payable) − Rs 0 (Recoverable) = Rs 66,666 Net Payable to Employee Note: If Rahul had not served his notice period, the employer could recover Rs 50,000 (one month’s salary) from the payable amount, reducing the net F&F to Rs 16,666. Retrenchment: Special Rules Under Industrial Relations Code 2020 Retrenchment refers to the termination of a worker’s service by the employer for economic or business reasons — not due to any fault or misconduct of the worker. It is one of the most regulated forms of termination in India. Key Rules for Retrenchment • Government permission: Establishments with 300 or more workers must obtain prior written permission from the appropriate government authority before retrenching any worker. • LIFO principle: The Last In, First Out rule applies — the last person hired in a particular category must be the first to be retrenched. • Notice requirement: The employer must give one month’s written notice or pay one month’s salary in lieu of notice. • Retrenchment compensation: 15 days’ average pay for every completed year of continuous service. This is in addition to the notice period pay. • Government reporting: The retrenchment must be reported to the appropriate government authority in the prescribed form. • Re-employment priority: If the employer recruits for the same or similar role within one year, retrenched workers must be given preference. Retrenchment Compensation Calculation Formula Retrenchment Compensation = 15 days average pay × completed years of service Average pay = Average of last 3 months’ wages (basic + DA) Example: A worker with 10 years of service and an average monthly wage of Rs 30,000 would receive: Compensation = (30,000 ÷ 26) × 15 × 10 = Rs 1,73,077 (approximately) Gratuity on Termination Gratuity is a statutory benefit paid by the employer to the employee as a reward for long and faithful service. Under the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 (now subsumed under the Code on Social Security 2020), gratuity is payable on termination, resignation, retirement, or death of the employee. Eligibility • Permanent employees: Must have completed a minimum of five years of continuous service. Service of 4 years and 240 days (or 190 days for seasonal establishments) is treated as five years. • Fixed-term contract employees: Under the new Labour Codes, fixed-term employees are entitled to pro-rata gratuity regardless of the length of service. The five-year minimum does not apply. • Exception: If the employee dies or becomes disabled, gratuity is payable regardless of service length. Gratuity Formula Calculation Gratuity = 15 × Last Drawn Salary (Basic + DA) × Years of Service ÷ 26 Each completed year of service counts. Months beyond 6 are rounded up to the next year. Tax exemption limit: Rs 20,00,000 (Rs 20 lakh) Example: An employee with 12 years and 8 months of service (rounded to 13 years) and a last drawn salary of Rs 40,000 (basic + DA): Gratuity = 15 × 40,000 × 13 ÷ 26 = Rs 3,00,000 Wrongful Termination: Consequences for Employers Wrongful termination (also called illegal or unfair termination) occurs when an employer terminates an employee without following the legally prescribed process, without valid cause, or in violation of statutory protections. The consequences can be severe: Consequence Details Reinstatement with Back Wages The Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal can order the employer to reinstate the employee with full back wages from the date of wrongful termination to the date of reinstatement. Compensation in Lieu of Reinstatement If reinstatement is not practical, the court can award compensation of up to 12 months’ wages to the employee. Penalty for Unfair Labour Practice Under the Industrial Relations Code 2020, the employer may face fines and penalties for engaging in unfair labour practices, including wrongful termination. Reputational Damage Wrongful termination cases damage the employer’s brand, make it harder to attract talent, and can lead to negative coverage on employer review platforms. Legal Costs and Management Time Labour disputes can take years to resolve. The legal costs, management time, and operational disruption far exceed the cost of following the correct process. The best protection against wrongful termination claims is a well-documented, transparent, and legally compliant process. Every step — from the show cause notice to the inquiry proceedings to the termination letter — must be recorded and preserved. Related Shashank Yadav Leave a Reply Cancel reply

title: Still waiting for a housing crash? It may be costing you
summary: Waiting for a housing crash before buying? Here's the real dollar cost of waiting, why most economists don't expect a 2008-style crash, and what to check instead.
body_text: A growing share of Americans say they're waiting for the housing market to crash so prices will go down before they make an offer on a home. But if a crash doesn't come (and most economists don't expect one) waiting could have a real cost: home prices have historically risen by about 3% to 4% a year, so the same house typically costs more the longer you wait, even before accounting for how mortgage rates might move. That doesn't mean you should buy before you're ready. It means "waiting for a crash" is a bet, not a plan, and it's worth understanding what that bet could actually cost. See how much you could borrow ...in as little as 3 minutes — no credit impact Why so many people are hoping for a crash According to recent survey data, about a third of Americans say they're actively hoping the housing market crashes. More than a quarter of non-homeowners believe a crash is their best way to afford a home. High home prices, combined with elevated mortgage rates, top the list of concerns driving that sentiment. It's an understandable reaction. National median home prices have kept climbing to new records even with rates well above where they sat a few years ago, and that combination has squeezed a lot of would-be buyers out of the market or onto the sidelines. But hoping for a crash and planning for one are different things. Most housing economists don't see the conditions that caused the 2008 crash repeating today. Inventory has been tight for years, not oversupplied, and current homeowners are, on average, in a much stronger equity position than they were heading into the last downturn. For context, home prices have been on a long upward march for decades , with only a handful of multi-year stretches of decline in that entire span, the 2008 crash being the most significant. What waiting actually costs, in dollars Here's an illustrative example using a $440,600 home, the recent national median, bought with 10% down. If you buy today at a 6.64% rate, your estimated principal and interest payment is about $2,543 a month, on a loan of roughly $396,540. If you wait a year and the same home appreciates at the historical average of about 4%, that same home would cost roughly $458,200. Putting 10% down on that higher price means a bigger loan, plus a larger cash down payment. Even if your rate stayed exactly the same, your monthly principal and interest payment would rise to around $2,645 a month, and you'd need about $1,760 more cash at closing. Example is for illustrative purposes only. Rates, payments, and total interest will vary based on credit profile, loan terms, and market conditions. Payments will also include local property taxes and homeowners insurance fees which are not included in this example. That's about $100 more a month and nearly $1,800 more upfront, just from waiting twelve months, in a market that keeps appreciating rather than crashing. Stretch that out, and the gap keeps compounding, since you're also making a year less progress on your loan balance and building a year less equity. See how much you could borrow ...in as little as 3 minutes — no credit impact But what if rates drop while you wait? This is the strongest counterargument to buying now, and it's worth taking seriously. If mortgage rates fall meaningfully, a lower rate could offset, or even outweigh, a higher purchase price. The catch is that lower rates tend to draw more buyers back into the market at the same time, which can push prices up faster, not slower. That's part of why affordability hasn't improved as much as some buyers expected even in stretches where rates have eased. To be clear, there's no reliable way to predict when, or how much, rates will move, which is exactly why waiting on a rate call is a bet rather than a strategy. If you already have a rate you're comfortable with today, mortgage rates could be refinanced later if they drop, assuming you can qualify for a new mortgage at that time. But a home price that's already appreciated generally isn't coming back down. Is it possible prices actually fall? Yes, home prices can, most definitely, fall. Real estate is cyclical, and local markets can and do soften, especially in areas with a lot of new construction or an oversupply of listings. National median prices can also dip temporarily. But a broad, 2008-style crash is a different scenario than a local correction, and betting your homebuying timeline on the former happening nationally is a much bigger gamble than most people realize. If your local market shows signs of cooling, that's a more reliable signal to watch than national crash predictions. Signs of a cooling market include price cuts, homes sitting longer, and rising inventory. Here's a more useful question than "will it crash?" Rather than trying to time a market crash, it's usually more productive to ask whether you can afford a home today, and whether waiting is likely to improve or worsen that math for your specific situation. That depends on your income stability, how much you have saved for a down payment , your credit profile , and how long you plan to stay in the home. A mortgage calculator can help estimate your costs with your actual numbers rather than a national average. Frequently asked questions about waiting for a housing crash Is the housing market going to crash? No one can say for sure. Most economists don't see the specific conditions that caused the 2008 crash present in today's market. Prices could soften in some local markets, but a broad national crash isn't the consensus expectation. How much does waiting to buy actually cost me? It depends on how much home prices and mortgage rates move while you wait. Using a historical appreciation rate of around 4% a year, waiting a year on a median-priced home can mean paying roughly $100 more a month and needing a larger cash down payment, even if your rate doesn't change. Should I wait for mortgage rates to drop before buying? There's no one-size-fits-all answer to this question. If rates drop later, after you've bought a home, you may be able to refinance into a lower rate. But the home price you locked in today may not come back down once it's appreciated. Waiting on a rate improvement that may not materialize carries its own risk. What's actually different between today's market and the 2008 crash? The 2008 crash was driven largely by risky lending standards and a subsequent wave of foreclosures that flooded the market with inventory. Today's housing shortage is largely a supply problem, not a lending or foreclosure problem. Are home prices guaranteed to keep rising? No. Local markets can soften, and national appreciation isn't guaranteed year to year. But historically, home prices have trended upward over time more often than they've fallen, which is part of why "waiting for a crash" is a bet rather than a sure thing. Bottom line about waiting for a housing market crash Hoping for a housing crash is understandable when home prices seem out of reach, but most economists don't expect one, and waiting could risk paying more later. Rather than basing your plans on a crash that may never come, it's usually more useful to figure out what you can actually afford today.
